jurisdiction.name: Congo
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The Republic of the Congo has no AI law or adopted AI strategy. Its AI governance rests on the 2019 personal data protection law, which includes a rule on automated decisions, with a national data protection commission created by a 2025 law but not yet staffed, and on the 2024 law creating the African AI Research Centre (CARIA) in Brazzaville, whose 2025 statutes mandate it to propose national AI strategies. A national AI strategy has been in drafting since May 2026.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
National Commission for Personal Data Protection
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. All records were read in the official gazette; the national AI strategy is still being drafted and is listed as a lead.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 29-2019 du 10 octobre 2019 portant protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on the protection of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Journal officiel n° 45-2019 of 7 November 2019 (law dated 10 October 2019; no separate entry-into-force date is stated). No decree appointing its members was found as of 2026-10-12.
instruments.summary: Congo's general personal data protection law, applying to automated and non-automated processing by public and private controllers on Congolese territory, with a supervisory commission to be created by a separate law. Article 13 bars court decisions assessing a person's behaviour from being based on automated processing that evaluates aspects of personality, and bars decisions with legal effects based solely on automated processing intended to define a profile or evaluate personality, with an exception for contract decisions where the person could present observations. Article 100 gives existing public-sector processing two years and other processing one year to comply.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law with an explicit automated decision-making and profiling rule (art. 13); governs AI training and use on personal data.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): official Journal officiel PDF on sgg.cg downloaded and read (pdftotext); JO n° 45-2019 of 7 November 2019, pp. 1404 ff.; art. 13 and arts. 100-101 read. Status note: effective_date left null. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): JO masthead 'N° 45 … Jeudi 7 novembre 2019' (PDF p.1; law at p.1404).

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 14-2024 du 23 mai 2024 portant création du centre africain de recherche en intelligence artificielle
instruments.english_title: Law No. 14-2024 of 23 May 2024 establishing the African Artificial Intelligence Research Centre
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Journal officiel n° 23-2024 of 6 June 2024 (law dated 23 May 2024; no separate entry-into-force date stated). The Council of Ministers approved the bill on 22 March 2022 (official Council of Ministers report), noting the centre was already operating in partnership with the UN Economic Commission for Africa. Statutes approved by Decree 2025-279.
instruments.summary: Creates the African Artificial Intelligence Research Centre (CARIA) in Brazzaville as a scientific and technical public administrative establishment with legal personality and financial autonomy, under the administrative and technical supervision of the digital economy minister and the scientific supervision of the research minister. Its missions include proposing national development strategies on AI and other emerging technologies, guiding AI use for Africa's economic and social development, promoting research in cybersecurity and personal data protection, training, and supporting AI start-ups. It is run by a steering committee and a directorate general whose heads are appointed by decree in Council of Ministers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding act of the national AI research body, which is mandated to propose national AI strategies.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): official Journal officiel PDF on sgg.cg downloaded and read (pdftotext); JO n° 23-2024 of 6 June 2024, arts. 1-9 read

instruments.official_title: Décret n° 2025-279 du 2 juillet 2025 portant approbation des statuts du centre africain de recherche en intelligence artificielle
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 2025-279 of 2 July 2025 approving the statutes of the African Artificial Intelligence Research Centre
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic (decree in Council of Ministers), on the report of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Journal officiel n° 35-2025 of 28 August 2025 (decree dated 2 July 2025). Note: the decree's visa cites Law 14-2024 as creating the 'centre de recherche en intelligence artificielle' (omitting 'africain').
instruments.summary: Approves the statutes of CARIA under article 8 of Law 14-2024, setting its missions, seat, duration and supervision, and the attributions, organisation and functioning of its steering committee and directorate general. The statutes restate the centre's mission to propose national development strategies on AI and emerging technologies and to promote research in cybersecurity and personal data protection, and organise its directorates (including research and cooperation).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Implementing decree organising the national AI research body.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): official Journal officiel PDF on sgg.cg downloaded and read (pdftotext); JO n° 35-2025 of 28 August 2025 pp. 1171 ff.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 5-2025 du 29 mars 2025 portant création de la commission nationale pour la protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 5-2025 of 29 March 2025 establishing the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (National Assembly and Senate); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Journal officiel n° 15-2025 of 10 April 2025 (law dated 29 March 2025; no separate entry-into-force date stated). Implementing decree on the commission's functioning and a decree appointing its members are required; neither was found in the gazette as of 2026-10-12.
instruments.summary: Creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNPD), an independent administrative authority with legal personality and financial autonomy seated in Brazzaville, as the supervisory authority under Law 29-2019. It receives prior notifications and complaints, carries out inspections, imposes sanctions on controllers, authorises cross-border transfers, gives opinions, advises those running or experimenting with personal data processing, and keeps a public register of processing. Its 16 members (designated by state institutions, the bar and civil society) serve five-year terms renewable once and may not receive instructions; its decisions are subject to appeal before the administrative courts.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Establishes the authority that enforces the data protection law, including its art. 13 rule on automated decisions and profiling.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): official Journal officiel PDF on sgg.cg downloaded and read (pdftotext); JO n° 15-2025 of 10 April 2025, pp. 502-504; all 20 articles read

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The Official Journal, the ministry responsible for posts, telecommunications and the digital economy, other ministries and the regulators were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for strategies, ethics, risk and assurance, public-sector rules, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sector rules, generative AI, drafts and consultations, international agreements, or past instruments. A national AI strategy and a 2030 digital strategy are still in preparation and listed under Leads; the ministry and government portals and whether the data protection commission's members have been appointed remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. postetelecom.gouv.cg, gouv.cg, adenumerique.cg and caria.cg unreachable; all records read in the Journal officiel on sgg.cg. Run resumed after a usage-limit interruption; the three earlier records were re-checked against their official PDFs (current_status corrected for Law 29-2019 and Law 14-2024). Congo Digital 2025 has no AI content (not recorded); Law 9-2026 (IDA financing with project AI clauses) not recorded. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Journal officiel (sgg.cg): Law 29-2019 (data protection, art. 13 automated decisions), Law 5-2025 (creating the data protection commission CNPD), Law 14-2024 (CARIA) and Decree 2025-279 (CARIA statutes) read in full; Decree 2019-150 approving the national digital economy strategy (Congo Digital 2025, annexed in JO n° 27-2019 of 4 July 2019) read: it contains no AI content, so it is not recorded. sgg.cg site search and the latest 2026 issues (n° 36-41) checked; the only other AI text found is a World Bank financing agreement annex (Law 9-2026, JO n° 36-2026) with project-level AI clauses, not recorded. No AI law, deepfake offence or AI bill found.; Government: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy: no national AI strategy adopted (drafting started May 2026, lead); 2030 digital strategy pending (lead). Ministry and government portals (postetelecom.gouv.cg, gouv.cg) could not be reached. No public-sector AI rules, procurement, ethics, generative-AI or index documents found.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found for education, health, justice, defence, finance, labour and interior AI documents.; Regulators: Data protection commission (CNPD) created by Law 5-2025 (recorded); no member appointment decree, guidance or decisions found. ARPCE (telecom regulator) site reachable but no AI document found (an AI/data regulation seminar was held in January 2026, no document). No AI documents from the cyber security agency, central bank (BEAC, regional) or standards body found.. Not reached: postetelecom.gouv.cg and gouv.cg (proxy 502); adenumerique.cg and caria.cg (connection failed). Could not verify: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy website and gouv.cg (unreachable); Whether CNPD members have been appointed or the commission's functioning decree adopted (none found via sgg.cg search). strategy, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
